facts: Supply the scheme people leave off (`example.com/mcp`) before every check below.
Checked first so it is the message shown. Wording only: the public-address check that actually keeps Cloud off private networks is the transport's, and runs regardless.
Zod still runs this after `.url()` fails; a throw here would escape `safeParse`.
The address a remote entry connects to. `mcp.json` often carries a bare `example.com/mcp`.

Users paste MCP server addresses the way they type them into a browser: `mcp.example.com/sse`, `example.com/mcp`, `localhost:3000/mcp`. `new URL` rejects the first two and misreads the last as a URL with the scheme `localhost:`, so every surface failed with "not a valid URL".
